current.subject: Brightline Media: recap of today's technical validation
current.body:
Hi Doug, Karen, Luis,

Thanks for the time today. Nia ran your viewing logs through the audience pipeline: dedupe took about 11 minutes for 380 million events on your sample day, and the attribution numbers looked about right to Karen at the 14 day window. Luis also saw failure alerts with a single automatic retry before anything pages him.

What's next:
- Ryan: one pager for Ann by Wednesday, October 7th.
- Nia: dedupe config and a note on late events tomorrow.
- Karen: list of your 60 segments, marking SQL vs spreadsheet.
- Open: your privacy team's view on joining viewing logs to subscriber records for opted out people. We can filter on a consent flag at ingestion, but whether the join is allowed is their call.

Nia also mentioned an aggregate only agency view that she could set up if you move to a pilot. No pilot has been agreed yet.

Ryan

original.subject: Recap from today's Apex validation session
original.body:
Hi Doug, Karen, and Luis,

Thanks for the time today. Here is where we landed.

What we showed: on your sample day, the dedupe ran in about 11 minutes for 380 million events, versus your current four hour job. Attribution ran with a 14 day window, and Karen said the numbers looked about right. Failure alerts go to your on call tool, with one automatic retry first.

From Apex:
- Nia will send the dedupe config and a note on late events tomorrow.
- I will send a one pager for Ann by Wednesday, October 7th.
- Nia will set up an aggregate only agency view as part of the pilot.

From you:
- Karen will send the list of the 60 segments, marking SQL versus spreadsheet.
- Doug will talk to Ann about budget ahead of November planning.

Still open: your privacy team's view on joining viewing logs to subscriber records for people who opted out. We can filter on a consent flag at ingestion, but the decision on the join is theirs.

Ryan
